subdomain: 4.5 Optimize token usage, latency, and cost-performance trade-offs

en.question: An assistant repeatedly sends the same long policy and unchanged tools within a supported cache lifetime. The policy meets the model's cache-length requirement, but every request prepends a unique correlation ID to the system text and cache reads remain zero. What should be changed first?

options.text: Choose a longer cache lifetime while keeping the unique ID before the policy.
options.note: A longer lifetime does not make different prefixes identical. The unique early value prevents reuse even though calls already occur within the supported lifetime.

options.text: Put the cache breakpoint after the entire message, including its unique user question.
options.note: A breakpoint after varying content does not create a stable reusable prefix. It leaves the correlation ID and changing question inside the material expected to match.

options.text: Lower the output budget and retain the existing system-text and cache layout.
options.note: Output generation settings do not repair an input-prefix mismatch. They can reduce generation length but will not turn the reported misses into policy-prefix hits.

options.text: Move the ID to the varying suffix, mark the stable prefix, and verify cache counters.
options.note: Caching requires an identical eligible prefix, ordered through tools, system, and messages. Keeping variable data after the stable policy boundary enables reuse, and usage counters verify whether it actually occurs.
